vocabulary.meaning_en: a thing you like more than another
vocabulary.note_en: Verb: prefer /prɪˈfɜː/ (stress on the second part).
vocabulary.example: My preference is tea, not coffee.

vocabulary.meaning_en: what you think or believe about something
vocabulary.example: In my opinion, the plan is good.

vocabulary.meaning_en: used for imaginary or conditional ideas, polite wishes and opinions
vocabulary.meaning_ar: فعل ناقص للشرط والتخيّل والتعبير المهذّب
vocabulary.example: I would like a cup of tea.
I'd like to go to the store.
I'd prefer to stay at home tonight.

vocabulary.meaning_en: would prefer to (followed by the base verb)
vocabulary.example: I'd rather walk than take the bus.

vocabulary.meaning_en: true only if something else happens
not real; only in your mind
a verb + -ing used like a noun (swimming, reading)
vocabulary.example: In "I like reading", reading is a gerund.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the base form of a verb, often with to (to go)
something you can prove is true
vocabulary.example: That's my opinion, not a fact.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the feeling that something is not true
vocabulary.example: She looked at me in disbelief.

fine_lines.title: would like vs would prefer vs would rather
fine_lines.explanation_ar: would like + to + المصدر. would prefer + to + المصدر (أو اسم). would rather + المصدر بدون to، ومع المقارنة نستخدم than.
fine_lines.explanation_en: would like + to + base verb. would prefer + to + base verb (or a noun). would rather + base verb with no to; to compare, use than.

examples.sentence: I would like to go home.
I would prefer to go by train.
I would rather sleep than watch TV.

fine_lines.title: opinion vs fact
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الحقيقة يمكن إثباتها. الرأي هو ما تعتقده ولا تستطيع إثباته؛ لذلك نستخدم would لتليين الرأي.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A fact can be proved. An opinion is what you think and can't prove, so we often use would to state it softly.

examples.sentence: I wouldn't believe anything he says.

expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to say what you want.
expressions.example: I'd like to ask a question.

expressions.meaning_en: I prefer one action to another.
expressions.example: I'd rather read a book than watch TV.

expressions.phrase: I wouldn't believe anything he says.
expressions.meaning_en: An opinion: I think he does not tell the truth.
expressions.example: Be careful. I wouldn't believe anything he says.

expressions.meaning_en: A soft way to give your opinion.
expressions.example: I would think that the shop is closed now.

grammar.title: S = State POP (Preference and Opinion)
grammar.explanation_ar: في طريقة SEAM، حرف S يعني State POP: التعبير عن التفضيل (Preference) والرأي (OPinion). نستخدم would لأنها تعبّر عن الشرط والتخيّل، أي ما نتمنّاه أو نتخيله وليس حقيقة مؤكدة 100%.
grammar.explanation_en: In the SEAM method, S means State POP: Preference and OPinion. We use would because it is conditional and imaginary: what we wish or imagine, not a 100% fact.
examples: I would like to go out. (preference)

grammar.title: Preference: would like / would prefer / would rather
grammar.explanation_ar: would like + to + المصدر. would prefer + to + المصدر أو اسم؛ وللمقارنة بين نشاطين: prefer + -ing + to + -ing. would rather + المصدر (بدون to) + than + المصدر.
grammar.explanation_en: would like + to + base verb. would prefer + to + base verb, or a noun; to compare two activities: prefer + -ing + to + -ing. would rather + base verb (no to) + than + base verb.
examples: I would like to visit Cairo.
I'd prefer the blue dress to the red one.
I prefer running to sitting at home.
I'd rather stay home than go out in the rain.

grammar.title: Opinion: would / wouldn't + base verb
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم would أو wouldn't + المصدر لإبداء رأي ليس حقيقة مؤكدة، وغالبًا مع believe و think.
grammar.explanation_en: Use would / wouldn't + base verb to give an opinion that is not a proven fact, often with believe and think.
examples: I would think he is at home now.
I would think that he wouldn't do something like that.

questions.question: In SEAM, "State POP" means stating your ___.
I'd rather ___ at home tonight.
questions.explanation_en: would rather + base verb, no to.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: I'd rather to walk than drive.
questions.explanation_en: would rather + base verb + than + base verb.

questions.question: "I wouldn't believe anything he says." This is ___.
questions.explanation_en: It is an opinion; it can't be proved.

questions.question: Why do we use "would" for preferences?
choices: It shows something imaginary or conditional.
questions.explanation_en: Would shows something imaginary or conditional.

questions.question: What is a gerund?
choices: a verb + -ing used as a noun
questions.explanation_en: A gerund is a verb + -ing used as a noun.

questions.question: What does "I'd" mean in "I'd prefer tea"?
What is a "preference"?
questions.explanation_en: A preference is something you like more.
